To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypertonic saline is an accurate and reproducible test of airway responsiveness in children.

bronchial challenge testing with ultrasonically generated 4.5 percent hypertonic saline is an effective method for assessing airway hyperresponsiveness in children with asthma and that the nebulization output of the ultrasonic nebulizer is an important determinant to the accuracy of bronchoconstriction induced by 4.5 % saline.

bronchial challenge tests with ultrasonically produced 4.5 percent saline in children are well tolerated by the children, but are less accurate than challenge tests with histamine or hyperventilation, and that increasing the nebulizer flow rate improves the accuracy of challenge tests with 4. 5 percent saline.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pathophysiology of asthma in children, particularly the role of airway hyperreactivity in the disease.
the study of the mechanisms of airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) in children and the relationship between airway inflammation and AHR.
the use of hypertonic saline in the diagnosis of mild asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bronchial challenge testing with hypertonic saline in children is a promising test, but further studies are needed before it will be accepted as a standard test of bronchial hyperresponsiveness in children.
bronchial challenge testing with 4. 5% saline is an acceptable test of bronchial hyperresponsiveness in children.

bronchial challenge testing with ultrasonically produced hypertonic saline is promising, but not yet ready to be recommended for use in children with asthma or in normal children as a diagnostic test of bronchial hyperresponsiveness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypertonic saline is an effective bronchial challenge agent for children with asthma, but the nebulizer used for its delivery is an important determinant for the accuracy of the test.
the ultrasonic nebulization technique with hypertonic saline is a promising new method to assess airway reactivity in children with mild bronchial asthma.
the hypertonic saline inhalation challenge test is a useful tool for assessing airway inflammation in children with asthma and may be used to assess the response to treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nebulization of hypertonic saline is a safe and well tolerated test of bronchial hyperresponsiveness in children.
hypertonic saline challenge is a safe and effective test for assessing bronchial hyperresponsiveness in children.
hypertonic saline is a promising new bronchial challenge agent in children.
